title: GDP
about: Gross domestic product in current US dollars: the most recent figure the World Bank has for each country, and a figure from elsewhere (see "others") for most of those it has none for.
estimate: No figure anywhere for these: their population times the median GDP per person (9,474 US$).

others.AI: 2023. United Nations national accounts, as republished by Worldometers. https://www.worldometers.info/gdp/anguilla-gdp/
others.AX: 2016. ÅSUB (Statistics Åland): about 1,280 million euros, at 1.11 US$ to the euro. https://www.asub.ax/sites/default/files/statistics/bnp_meddelande_2016_.pdf
others.BL: 2014. IEDOM and AFD: 367 million euros, at 1.33 US$ to the euro. https://www.iedom.fr/IMG/pdf/note_pib_saint-barth-2014_afd_iedom.pdf
others.BQ: 2022. Statistics Netherlands: Bonaire 662, Sint Eustatius 92 and Saba 49 million US$. https://www.cbs.nl/en-gb/figures/detail/84789ENG
others.CK: 2023. United Nations national accounts, as republished by Worldometers. https://www.worldometers.info/gdp/cook-islands-gdp/
others.FK: 2024. Falkland Islands Government national accounts: 288 million pounds, at 1.28 US$ to the pound. https://en.mercopress.com/2025/08/11/falklands-gross-national-income-per-capita-58-749-in-2024-fig-national-accounts
others.GF: 2023. IEDOM: about 5.0 billion euros, at 1.08 US$ to the euro. https://www.iedom.fr/IMG/pdf/iedom_ra_24_-chiffres-cles.pdf
others.GG: 2023. World Bank figure for the Channel Islands (12.51 billion US$), shared by the islands' own GDP: Jersey 6,575 and Guernsey 3,488 million pounds. https://www.islandfm.com/news/guernsey/guernseys-economy-worth-3-48-billion1/
others.GI: 2023. Government of Gibraltar: 2,901 million pounds in 2023/24, at 1.26 US$ to the pound. https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/uploads/statistics/2025/National%20Accounts/GDP%20Estimates%202010%20-%2011%20-%202024-25.pdf
others.GP: 2023. IEDOM: about 10.4 billion euros, at 1.08 US$ to the euro. https://www.iedom.fr/IMG/pdf/iedom_ra_24_-chiffres-cles.pdf
others.JE: 2023. World Bank figure for the Channel Islands (12.51 billion US$), shared by the islands' own GDP: Jersey 6,575 and Guernsey 3,488 million pounds. https://www.gov.je/News/2024/Pages/MeasuringJerseysEconomy2023.aspx
others.KP: 2024. Bank of Korea estimate of North Korea's nominal gross national income: 44.4 trillion won. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/amp/foreignaffairs/northkorea/20250829/n-korean-economy-logs-fastest-growth-in-8-years-in-2024-bok
others.MQ: 2023. IEDOM: about 10.1 billion euros, at 1.08 US$ to the euro. https://www.iedom.fr/IMG/pdf/iedom_ra_24_-chiffres-cles.pdf
others.MS: 2023. United Nations national accounts, as republished by Worldometers. https://www.worldometers.info/gdp/montserrat-gdp/
others.NU: 2019. Asian Development Bank: 47 million New Zealand dollars, at 0.66 US$ to the dollar. https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/institutional-document/752631/niue-country-classification.pdf
others.PM: 2015. IEDOM and AFD: 240 million euros, at 1.11 US$ to the euro. https://www.iedom.fr/IMG/pdf/cp_pib_spm.pdf
others.RE: 2023. INSEE: 23.2 billion euros, at 1.08 US$ to the euro. https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/2012723
others.SH: 2024. St Helena Statistics Office: 40.7 million pounds in 2024/25, at 1.28 US$ to the pound. https://www.sainthelena.gov.sh/statistical-update-gross-domestic-product-2425/
others.TW: 2025. DGBAS (Taiwan's statistics office): GDP per person of US$39,477 in 2025, times the population. https://ocacnews.net/article/418912
others.VG: 2023. United Nations national accounts, as republished by Worldometers. https://www.worldometers.info/gdp/british-virgin-islands-gdp/
others.WF: 2019. IEOM: 22.6 billion CFP francs (189.4 million euros), at 1.12 US$ to the euro. https://www.ieom.fr/IMG/pdf/cp_pib_wf_2019_vf.pdf
others.YT: 2021. IEDOM: 3.1 billion euros, at 1.18 US$ to the euro. https://www.iedom.fr/IMG/pdf/iedom_ra_24_-chiffres-cles.pdf

note: France's World Bank figure includes its five overseas departments (RE, GP, MQ, GF, YT) and Finland's includes Åland (AX). They are on the map on their own as well, so about 0.05% of the world's GDP is counted twice.
